-- guitar teacher schema (SQLite-compatible)

PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;

create table teacher (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  phone TEXT
);

create table student (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  phone TEXT,
  date_of_birth DATE,
  skill_level TEXT CHECK (skill_level IN ('beginner','intermediate','advanced')),
  enrolled_at DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT (date('now'))
);

create table lesson (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  teacher_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  student_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  scheduled_at DATETIME NOT NULL,
  duration_minutes INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 60,
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'scheduled' CHECK (status IN ('scheduled','completed','cancelled','no-show')),
  notes TEXT,
  location TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'in-person' CHECK (location IN ('in-person','online')),
  foreign key (teacher_id) references teacher(id),
  foreign key (student_id) references student(id)
);

create table material (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  lesson_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (type IN ('song','technique','exercise','theory')),
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  description TEXT,
  homework INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  foreign key (lesson_id) references lesson(id)
);

create table package (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  lesson_count INTEGER NOT NULL,
  price NUMERIC NOT NULL,
  validity_days INTEGER NOT NULL
);

create table student_package (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  student_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  package_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  lessons_remaining INTEGER NOT NULL,
  purchased_at DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT (date('now')),
  expires_at DATE NOT NULL,
  foreign key (student_id) references student(id),
  foreign key (package_id) references package(id)
);

create table invoice (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  student_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  student_package_id INTEGER,
  amount NUMERIC NOT NULL,
  issued_at DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT (date('now')),
  due_at DATE NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unpaid' CHECK (status IN ('unpaid','paid','overdue')),
  foreign key (student_id) references student(id),
  foreign key (student_package_id) references student_package(id)
);

create table payment (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  invoice_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  amount NUMERIC NOT NULL,
  method TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (method IN ('cash','card','venmo','bank transfer','other')),
  paid_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  foreign key (invoice_id) references invoice(id)
);
 Give me a sqlite select statement that answers the question using the guitar teacher schema. Only respond with sqlite syntax. If there is an error do not explain it!

questionResults.question: Which students have lessons scheduled in the next 7 days?
questionResults.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT s.name, s.email, s.phone
FROM student s
JOIN lesson l ON s.id = l.student_id
WHERE l.scheduled_at BETWEEN date('now') AND date('now', '+7 days')
  AND l.status = 'scheduled';

questionResults.question: Which students have unpaid invoices and how much is outstanding for each?
questionResults.sql:
SELECT 
    s.name AS student_name,
    SUM(i.amount) AS outstanding_amount
FROM 
    student AS s
JOIN 
    invoice AS i ON s.id = i.student_id
WHERE 
    i.status = 'unpaid'
GROUP BY 
    s.id;

questionResults.question: Which students have overlapping lessons?
questionResults.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT s1.name AS student_name
FROM lesson l1
JOIN lesson l2 ON l1.student_id = l2.student_id AND l1.id <> l2.id
JOIN student s1 ON l1.student_id = s1.id
WHERE (l1.scheduled_at <= l2.scheduled_at AND l1.scheduled_at + l1.duration_minutes * 60 > l2.scheduled_at)
   OR (l2.scheduled_at <= l1.scheduled_at AND l2.scheduled_at + l2.duration_minutes * 60 > l1.scheduled_at);
questionResults.friendlyResponse: No students have overlapping lessons based on the information you provided.

questionResults.question: For each teacher, list their top 2 students by number of completed lessons and the teacher's average duration for completed lessons.
questionResults.sql:
WITH CompletedLessons AS (
  SELECT
    teacher_id,
    student_id,
    COUNT(*) AS completed_count
  FROM
    lesson
  WHERE
    status = 'completed'
  GROUP BY
    teacher_id,
    student_id
),
TopStudents AS (
  SELECT
    teacher_id,
    student_id,
    completed_count,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY teacher_id ORDER BY completed_count DESC, student_id) AS rn
  FROM
    CompletedLessons
),
TeacherAverageDuration AS (
  SELECT
    teacher_id,
    AVG(duration_minutes) AS avg_duration
  FROM
    lesson
  WHERE
    status = 'completed'
  GROUP BY
    teacher_id
)
SELECT
  t.name AS teacher_name,
  s.name AS student_name,
  ts.completed_count,
  tad.avg_duration
FROM
  TopStudents ts
JOIN
  teacher t ON ts.teacher_id = t.id
JOIN
  student s ON ts.student_id = s.id
JOIN
  TeacherAverageDuration tad ON ts.teacher_id = tad.teacher_id
WHERE
  ts.rn <= 2;

questionResults.question: Which students have packages that will expire within the next 7 days and also have unpaid invoices?
questionResults.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT s.name
FROM student s
JOIN student_package sp ON s.id = sp.student_id
JOIN invoice i ON s.id = i.student_id
WHERE sp.expires_at BETWEEN date('now') AND date('now', '+7 days')
  AND i.status = 'unpaid';
questionResults.friendlyResponse: There are currently no students with packages expiring within the next 7 days who also have unpaid invoices.

questionResults.question: Which invoices have partial payments?
questionResults.sql:
SELECT i.*
FROM invoice i
JOIN payment p ON i.id = p.invoice_id
GROUP BY i.id
HAVING SUM(p.amount) < i.amount;
questionResults.friendlyResponse: The invoices with partial payments are invoice ID 4 and invoice ID 6.

questionResults.question: List students whose no-show rate is greater than 25%.
questionResults.sql:
SELECT s.id, s.name, s.email
FROM student s
JOIN lesson l ON s.id = l.student_id
GROUP BY s.id, s.name, s.email
HAVING (SUM(CASE WHEN l.status = 'no-show' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(l.id)) > 25;
questionResults.friendlyResponse: The student who has a no-show rate greater than 25% is Kai Barnes, and you can contact them at kai.barnes@example.com.
